title: Dramatis Personae

teacherSummary.text: The cast list divides Verona into the Prince's family (Escalus, his kinsmen Paris and Mercutio), the house of Montague (Montague, Lady Montague, Romeo, Benvolio and servants) and the house of Capulet (Capulet, Lady Capulet, Juliet, Tybalt, the Nurse and servants), with two Franciscan friars and an apothecary outside both. The scenes are Verona and Mantua.

context.history: Verona and Mantua were real cities in northern Italy; Italy was, for English audiences of the 1590s, a place of passion, feuds and fashionable duelling. The story came to Shakespeare through Arthur Brooke's English poem of 1562.

significance: Reading the cast first lets students see the feud's structure: two houses 'at variance', each with servants who fight for them, and a few figures (the Prince's kin, the Friar) who might bridge or break the divide.
discussionQuestions: Have you ever belonged to a group that had a rival group? How did that rivalry affect friendships?
